title: Wreak
summary: WREAK, verb transitive [G. The sense is to drive or throw, to dash with violence.] 1. To execute; to inflict; to hurl or drive; as, to wreak vengeance on an enemy. On me let death wreak all his rage.

inlines.v: WREAK, verb transitive [G. The sense is to drive or throw, to dash with violence.] 1. To execute; to inflict; to hurl or drive; as, to wreak vengeance on an enemy. On me let death wreak all his rage. 2. To revenge. Come wreak his loss, whom bootless ye complain. Anothers wrongs to wreak upon thyself. [This latter sense is nearly or quite obsolete.] WREAK, for reck. To care, is a mistake. WREAK, noun Revenge; vengeance; furious passion.
